notes:
Applied the single low finding from docs/build/reviews/B0.5/verify2-core-polish.json exactly as specified.

Fix (src/Wakeel.Core/Services/OfficialNumberService.cs, IssueCoreAsync): added `if (today < row.LastDate.Date) throw new InvalidOperationException(\"official numbering refused: date is earlier than the last issued number\");` inside the retry loop, immediately after `row` is obtained/reloaded (both on the initial fetch and after every `ReloadAsync` in the catch block) and before `row.LastSeq >= MaxSequence`/`row.LastSeq += 1`. This re-evaluates the watermark on every attempt using the row's own (possibly just-reloaded) LastDate, closing the gap where the pre-loop cross-year MaxAsync check (kept unchanged) only proved the date wasn't backdated at the instant it ran, before any retry. A retry only ever occurs because another context raced this exact (kind, year) row (per IsSequenceRaceException's scoping), so the reload always refreshes row.LastDate to whatever that other context just committed — the recheck now catches a losing context that would otherwise unconditionally overwrite a later committed date with its own earlier one.

Test added: NumberingTests.Issue_WhenAnotherContextCommitsALaterDateWhileThisOneRaces_TheRetryRefuses_InsteadOfRegressingLastDate, reproducing the exact interleaving from the finding (B reads the watermark, A commits a later date, B loses the concurrency race, reloads, and must now refuse rather than regress official_numbers.last_date).

Design note on the test's engineering: a live two-connection interleaving cannot deliver this ordering deterministically on this database — a second connection's BeginTransaction blocks against (and times out on) a first connection's already-open transaction here regardless of isolation level, confirmed empirically (first attempt at this test, using a real second DbSession/transaction for context A, failed with SqliteException 'database is locked' at BeginTransactionAsync, consistent with the existing INSERT-race test's own documented finding that live overlap doesn't work on this setup). So the test uses one connection: a DbCommandInterceptor detects context B's own MaxAsync watermark query completing (matching command text containing both \"official_numbers\" and \"MAX\") and, at that exact moment — before B's retry loop reads or writes the row — runs an EF Core ExecuteUpdateAsync directly on B's own already-open transaction to land the later date, standing in for \"another context's commit\" landing at precisely that instant. B's own tracked row is pre-pinned stale (same technique as the existing Issue_WhenAnotherContextIssuedInBetween_IsRetried_AndTheNumbersDiffer test) so B's first SaveChanges genuinely loses the optimistic-concurrency check and reloads, exercising the real code path added by the fix.

Verified non-vacuous: temporarily reverted the fix (removed the new check) and reran only this test — it failed with \"No exception was thrown\" (the pre-fix code silently returned a result instead of refusing), confirming the test would have caught the exact bug the review flagged. Fix was then restored (confirmed identical to the applied version) before the final full-suite run.
